answer: A numbered tide gauge stands on a harbor post; an opal float riding it is the proof. At low tide the holder photographs the float against the gauge, with a yarrow-dyed rope marking the waterline and date. Two verifiers visit within 24 hours and match the float and rope mark; a float never seen at the gauge, or a duplicate number, locks the account and burns its deposit. One visit is cheap, but 100 fakes need 100 gauges and 100 harbor trips.
